sentences.text: CORAM:HONOURABLE MS. JUSTICE S.V. PINTO
Date : 16/02/2024  ORAL ORDER 1.
This application has been filed by the State challenging the orders dated 27.10.2022, 30.10.2023 and 10.11.2023 passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO), Rajkot in Sessions Case No.10 of 2016.

2. The brief facts that emerge from the record of the case are as under:
2.1.

That the complainant has filed FIR No.I-C.R.No.67 of 2015 on 14.08.2015 against the respondent herein for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(b)(l)(n),
354(a) and 506(2) of the IPC.
That the charge sheet came to be filed and the said offence came to be registered as Sessions Case No. 10 of 2016.

That the evidence of the prosecution is being recorded by the learned Trial Court and an application at Exh.

sentences.text:
1 285 was preferred by the Special Prosecutor for examining two witnesses namely Mr.M.M.Jadeja,
Police Inspector, Mahila Police Station, Rajkot and Ms.Ranjanben Sureshbhai Parekh, Principal,
Anandpar Primary School, Anandpar.

2.3 That the learned advocate for the respondent made an endorsement below the application stating that the complainant and the prosecution are trying to delay the case and has raised objections; however, has endorsed that the prosecution may examine these two witnesses on condition that the prosecution may not examine any other witnesses.

That the learned Trial Court,
after hearing the parties, rejected the application by order dated 27.10.2023.
2.4. That thereafter, the Special Public Prosecutor made an application at Exh.293 stating that they wanted to challenge the said order before this Court and hence, necessary time be granted.
That the learned trial Court rejected the application made by the Special Public Prosecutor.

That the learned Trial Court, thereafter, passed the order below Exh.1 closing the evidence of the prosecution by an order dated 10.11.2023.
3.

That all the three orders have been challenged by the State mainly stating that there are sufficient evidences, which are NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/208/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined yet to be put on record in the case which is suffice to show the involvement of the respondent herein in the commission of crime.

That under Section 311 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the learned Trial Court may summon any material witness or examine person present for the just decision and hence, the application be allowed in the interest of justice.

4. Heard learned APP Ms. Jirga Jhaveri for the applicant - State, learned advocate Ms. Ketki Jha for the original complainant and learned advocate Mr.Pratik Jasani for the respondent herein - accused.
4.1.

Learned APP Ms. Jirga Jhaveri for the applicant - State has submitted a letter dated 15.02.2024 by the Special Public Prosecutor to the Public Prosecutor of this Court and the same is taken on record.

Learned APP has submitted that besides the two witnesses mentioned in the application at Exh.285, the prosecution is seeking examination of another witness, who is the District Education Officer, Rajkot.

4.2. Learned advocate Mr. Pratik Jasani for the respondent herein - accused has submitted that as per the endorsement made below Exh.285, the learned advocate for the respondent - accused has clearly admitted and had given consent to examine these two witnesses, even though, witness namely Ranjanben Sureshbhai Parekh, Principal, Anandpar Primary NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/208/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined School, Anandpar was sought to be examined and an application at Exh.213 was given earlier, but,
the same was rejected by the learned Trial Court and the same was not challenged.
Learned advocate further submits that the matter is of the year 2015.

That by order dated 10.06.2022, this Court has passed an order in Criminal Misc. Application No. 1 of 2019 in Criminal Revision Application No. 1268 of 2018 and has directed the learned Trial Court to complete the trial within a period of six months from the date of receipt of the order.

It was categorically mentioned in the State Of Gujarat vs Ratubhai Raydhanbhai Chavda on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69709937/
2 order that it is expected from the concerned trial Court that no extension from the High Court shall be granted to complete such proceedings.

sentences.text: Learned advocate has further submitted that as per the order passed by this Court on 10.06.2022, the learned Trial Court ought to have completed the trial by 10.12.2022, but, till today, the trial has not been completed and in view of the above, necessary orders may be passed so that the matter is disposed as early as possible.

5. Without going into the details and in the interest of justice and as the learned advocate for the respondent herein - accused has conceded to examine the witnesses and also keeping in mind the order dated 10.06.2022 passed by this Court in Criminal Misc. Application No. 1 of 2019 in Criminal Revision Application No. 1268 of 2018, the present NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/208/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined application is allowed.
The learned Trial Court is directed to examine both the witnesses on the same day at the earliest as fiexed by the learned Trial Court.
The learned Trial Court is further directed to strictly adhere to the directions given by this Court in Criminal Misc. Application No. 1 of 2019 in Criminal Revision Application No. 1268 of 2018.
It is clarified that only the two witnesses sought to be examined in the application at Exh.285 will be examined by the learned Trial Court.
6. In view of the above, present application stands disposed of.
(S. V. PINTO,J) F.S.KAZI....
